questions.question: The root of b765 is not ready. (7)'s build ran after PLACE-papers' pre-root push and before the root, as the misses read's item (9) orders, and reads AS WANTED: PLACE-project-set at 464ec6e6, private, 35 files from PLACE-papers d2d8b00f and the relay 5ca769db. The seat had pushed the relay's pre-root commits before the build, so the builder's three relay banks, data/b765_project_set_build.json, data/b765_project_set_build.txt and data/b765_project_set_verify.txt, stand untracked, and root part 1 reads 150 of 153 banks clean and equal at HEAD. The root wants every bank it names committed and HEAD equal to the remote's main, and committing the three puts HEAD past the remote. The relay's main moves only by the gated push from a push branch the one-call tool makes. The branch push-b765-preroot stands at 5ca769db, the branch route makes a branch and moves none, and push-b765-record and push-b765-closing are the branches of steps [19] and [25]. N5 lists the branches removed, and push-b765-preroot is not among them (data/b765_ferry.txt :134). No route of the act's tools passes here without your word. How does the close go on?

options.label: Remake push-b765-preroot (Recommended)
options.description: The local push-b765-preroot, merged into main and never pushed under its own name, deleted by the one-call tool's route; the three banks committed as a third pre-root commit with its step row; the branch made again at that commit; the gated push, main read back; then the root and the close as ordered. The delete stands beyond N5's list of branches removed, on your word; the branch stands again at the close, and the closing message names the delete.

options.label: Halt the close at the root
options.description: The root not computed and the three banks left untracked; steps [14] to [25] carried to the next ruling with the build named, as b757's close was carried at [22]. The relay's main stays at 5ca769db and PLACE-papers' at d2d8b00f; the rows found after the lock stay in the seat's scratch source for that ruling.
